Waiting for better models is a valid approach in the current climate, however I suspect the looping will only be reduced not eliminated entirely. For long-running agentic orchestrators if looping happens once in a blue moon then just having a timeout on an opencode session seems fine, however if it happens with a bit more frequency then it would waste lots of time/resources and loop detection / remedy would be useful and worth implementing. In general, generating workarounds for common issues when working with LLMs does seem in scope iff those issues are common enough and exist across providers.

I am curious about repetition penalty based on the context you feed into an agent - I don't think this currently happens, and repetition penalties are only on the llm's output, when you feed in context from an agentic session, naturally the llm has no way of determining what was ITS previous input or what is part of a prompt etc. it's all just mixed together. This PR is a targeted portability refactor that replaces three `Bun.sleep()` calls with `sleep` aliased from `node:timers/promises`'s `setTimeout`, removing a dependency on the Bun-specific global API in favour of a Node.js-standard equivalent that Bun also supports. Key points: - The replacement (`import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises"`) is behaviourally identical to `Bun.sleep` for the one-argument `sleep(ms)` usage here. - Both changed files — the TUI workspace-list dialog and the control-plane SSE event loop — use the new import consistently. - The `node:timers/promises` `setTimeout` accepts an optional `AbortSignal` (3rd argument) that `Bun.sleep` lacks; this opens the door to making the `workspaceEventLoop` in `workspace.ts` more responsive to `stop.abort()` without any extra error-handling overhead, since the existing `catch` at the call site already handles `AbortError`.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- Safe to merge — the replacement is functionally equivalent and the only actionable note is an additive improvement. - The diff is minimal (3 call-sites, 2 import lines), the two APIs are semantically identical for the `sleep(ms)` single-argument usage, and `node:timers/promises` is available in Bun. The sole observation is a style-level suggestion to forward the existing `AbortSignal` to `sleep()` now that the API supports it, which would improve graceful shutdown responsiveness but is not a correctness issue. - No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/dialog-workspace-list.tsx | Replaces `Bun.sleep(1000)` with `sleep` aliased from `node:timers/promises`'s `setTimeout`; single-line change with no behavioural difference. | | packages/opencode/src/control-plane/workspace.ts | Replaces two `Bun.sleep` calls in the SSE event-loop retry path with `setTimeout as sleep` from `node:timers/promises`; functionally equivalent, but the `stop` AbortSignal is not forwarded to the new sleep calls, leaving a small window where the loop continues sleeping after abort is requested. |

Greptile Summary

This PR removes Bun-specific APIs from the TUI layer to improve portability: `Bun.write()` is swapped out for the existing `Filesystem.write()` utility in the session export flow, and `BunWebSocketData` type is removed from `worker.ts` in favour of an inferred return type. The `await server.stop(true)` fix in `shutdown()` is a genuine correctness improvement — the stop call was previously fire-and-forget, meaning the worker could signal completion before the HTTP server had fully released its port. **Key changes:** - `Bun.write(filepath, transcript)` → `Filesystem.write(filepath, transcript)` in two places in the session export handler — clean substitution, `Filesystem` was already imported. - `BunWebSocketData` type import removed from `hono/bun`; `server` is now typed as `Awaited>`, which is equivalent but Bun-agnostic. - `server.stop(true)` in `shutdown()` is now properly awaited, ensuring the server closes before the worker completes shutdown. - `server = await Server.listen(input)` adds a redundant `await` — `Server.listen` is a synchronous function, so the `await` is a no-op. It's harmless but slightly misleading.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge — changes are portable replacements with no functional regressions; the one genuine fix (awaiting `server.stop`) improves correctness. - All three changes are straightforward and low-risk. `Filesystem.write` is functionally identical to `Bun.write` for string content, and the type change is correct. The only imprecision is `await Server.listen(input)` on a synchronous function, which is a harmless no-op but slightly misleading. - No files require special attention, though `worker.ts` line 122 has a redundant `await` worth cleaning up.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/worker.ts | Removes `BunWebSocketData` type import, infers the server type via `Awaited>`, and correctly awaits `server.stop()` in shutdown. The `await Server.listen(input)` is a redundant no-op since `Server.listen` is synchronous. | | packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/index.tsx | Clean drop-in replacement of `Bun.write()` with `Filesystem.write()`. The `Filesystem` utility was already imported, and the function signatures are compatible (both accept a string path and string content). No issues found. |

In case someone is struggling with this, here's a self-contained fix. No need to read through all the comments above. Cheers, and happy coding!

## What happened

Anthropic sent a legal request and the official `opencode-anthropic-auth` plugin was removed (PR #18186). This broke Claude Pro/Max OAuth login in OpenCode.

## The community fix (with a tweak)

[@thehugeman](https://github.com/thehugeman) published a community replacement: [`@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community). It restores the OAuth flow, **but** it ships with outdated OAuth endpoints (`console.anthropic.com`) that Anthropic has since moved to `platform.claude.com`. This causes the **"invalid code"** error when you try to log in (see [issue #2](https://github.com/thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community/issues/2) on that repo for details).

The fix below downloads the plugin, patches the URLs, and saves it as a **local file** so opencode can't overwrite it.

## Steps

**1. Create a local plugins directory:**

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins
```

**2. Download the plugin and patch it in one shot:**

```bash
curl -s https://registry.npmjs.org/@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community/latest | \
  node -e "const j=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf8')); process.stdout.write(j.dist.tarball)" | \
  xargs curl -sL | tar -xzO package/index.mjs | \
  sed 's/console\.anthropic\.com/platform.claude.com/g' \
  > ~/.config/opencode/plugins/anthropic-auth.mjs
```

> If you prefer to do it manually, grab `index.mjs` from the [repo](https://github.com/thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community) and replace all 5 occurrences of `console.anthropic.com` with `platform.claude.com`.

**3. Add the local plugin to your `opencode.json`** (usually at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`):

Add `"./plugins/anthropic-auth.mjs"` to your `plugin` array. If you previously had the npm package, replace it:

```json
{
  "plugin": [
    "./plugins/anthropic-auth.mjs"
  ]
}
```

> If you haven't used the community plugin before and don't have a `plugin` array yet, just add one.

**4. Restart opencode and connect your account:**

1. Launch `opencode`
2. Press `/` and type `connect` (or run the `/connect` command)
3. Select **Anthropic** as the provider
4. Choose **Claude Pro/Max**
5. A browser window will open. Authorize with your Anthropic account
6. Copy the authorization code from the browser and paste it back into the terminal
7. That's it, you should now be connected

## Why a local file instead of the npm package?

If you reference the npm package directly in `opencode.json`, opencode can re-download and overwrite it from its cache at any time, undoing the URL fix. A local plugin file is fully under your control and survives updates.

Additionally, you definitely don't want to use an "unknown" package in your local environment, so this protects you from any future "hacks" or "changes" made to the [`@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community) package, in case it were to happen.

## Disclaimer

This may violate Anthropic's Terms of Service. Use at your own risk.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

**Potential Duplicate Found:**

- **PR #14341**: [feat: add provider openWebUI](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/14341)
  - This PR is directly related as it's the original work that PR #18306 is built upon. The current PR (#18306) explicitly mentions it builds on PR #14341.

The current PR (#18306) appears to be an updated or refactored version of the Open WebUI provider feature originally introduced in PR #14341. The description acknowledges this relationship, so these two PRs are related but the current one seems to be a successor/improvement to the earlier work.

It would be great if this was solved somehow. But, at this point, it looks like this is for Ollama to fix.

Ollama has two APIs: their native API, and the OpenAI API.

The Ollama native API has a way to set the TTL for a model, and it works. But OpenCode does not use the native API.

The OpenAI API also has a way to set the TTL, but Ollama ignores it, because it does not have a full implementation of the OpenAI API. This is the API that OpenCode uses.

> In case someone is struggling with this, here's a self-contained fix. No need to read through all the comments above. Cheers, and happy coding!
> 
> ## What happened
> Anthropic sent a legal request and the official `opencode-anthropic-auth` plugin was removed (PR [#18186](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18186)). This broke Claude Pro/Max OAuth login in OpenCode.
> 
> ## The community fix (with a tweak)
> [@thehugeman](https://github.com/thehugeman) published a community replacement: [`@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community). It restores the OAuth flow, **but** it ships with outdated OAuth endpoints (`console.anthropic.com`) that Anthropic has since moved to `platform.claude.com`. This causes the **"invalid code"** error when you try to log in (see [issue #2](https://github.com/thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community/issues/2) on that repo for details).
> 
> The fix below downloads the plugin, patches the URLs, and saves it as a **local file** so opencode can't overwrite it.
> 
> ## Steps
> **1. Create a local plugins directory:**
> 
> mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins
> **2. Download the plugin and patch it in one shot:**
> 
> curl -s https://registry.npmjs.org/@thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community/latest | \
>   node -e "const j=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf8')); process.stdout.write(j.dist.tarball)" | \
>   xargs curl -sL | tar -xzO package/index.mjs | \
>   sed 's/console\.anthropic\.com/platform.claude.com/g' \
>   > ~/.config/opencode/plugins/anthropic-auth.mjs
> > If you prefer to do it manually, grab `index.mjs` from the [repo](https://github.com/thehugeman/opencode-anthropic-auth-community) and replace all 5 occurrences of `console.anthropic.com` with `platform.claude.com`.
> 
> **3. Add the local plugin to your `opencode.json`** (usually at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`):
> 
> Add `"./plugins/anthropic-auth.mjs"` to your `plugin` array. If you previously had the npm package, replace it:
> 
> {
>   "plugin": [
>     "./plugins/anthropic-auth.mjs"
>   ]
> }
> > If you haven't used the community plugin before and don't have a `plugin` array yet, just add one.
> 
> **4. Restart opencode and connect your account:**
> 
> 1. Launch `opencode`
> 2. Press `/` and type `connect` (or run the `/connect` command)
> 3. Select **Anthropic** as the provider
> 4. Choose **Claude Pro/Max**
> 5. A browser window will open. Authorize with your Anthropic account
> 6. Copy the authorization code from the browser and paste it back into the terminal
> 7. That's it, you should now be connected
> 
> ## Why a local file instead of the npm package?
> If you reference the npm package directly in `opencode.json`, opencode can re-download and overwrite it from its cache at any time, undoing the URL fix. A local plugin file is fully under your control and survives updates.
> 
> ## Disclaimer
> This may violate Anthropic's Terms of Service. Use at your own risk.

Built on OpenClaw, we run 9 agents across two machines coordinated through shared rooms on GroupMind. Each agent gets its own worktree for isolation, similar to what m13v describes, but coordination happens through a message stream rather than a conductor process.

The key difference from tmux-based orchestration: our agents are decoupled. They poll a shared room for tasks and post results back. If one crashes, the others keep working. No central conductor that is a single point of failure.

For workspace isolation specifically: worktrees work well for parallel feature branches, but we also use external state (memory files, config directories) so agent context survives across sessions. The workspace is disposable, the coordination state is not.

IDE Agent Kit (https://github.com/ThinkOffApp/ide-agent-kit) handles the webhook relay and room polling if you want to try this pattern with your own agents.

This PR removes two direct Bun API dependencies (`Bun.spawn` in MCP and `Bun.$` in session prompt) and replaces them with the existing portable `Process` utility. The MCP change is a clean, equivalent refactor. The session prompt change introduces a subtle but impactful issue. - **MCP (`index.ts`)**: `Bun.spawn` + manual stdout parsing replaced by `Process.lines()`. Functionally identical; `Process.lines` splits on `\r?\n` and filters empty strings, which correctly handles `pgrep -P`'s one-PID-per-line output. A minor style improvement (`!pids.includes()` over `pids.indexOf() === -1`) is also included. - **Session prompt (`prompt.ts`)**: `Bun.$\`${{ raw: cmd }}\`` replaced by `Process.text([cmd], { shell: sh, nothrow: true })`. The shell is obtained via `Shell.preferred()`, but `Shell.preferred()` does not filter out POSIX-incompatible shells — `fish` and `nu` are both valid returns. `Shell.acceptable()` exists precisely to handle this and is already used by the bash tool for the same reason. On a system where `$SHELL=fish`, every template shell substitution will silently produce an empty string, which is a user-visible regression. - **Error visibility**: the old code surfaced spawn failures as a `"Error executing command: …"` string in the template. The new path returns an empty string on failure, losing that diagnostic signal.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge for most users, but will silently break template shell commands for users with fish or nu as their default shell. - The MCP change is clean and correct. The prompt change has a real correctness issue: using `Shell.preferred()` instead of `Shell.acceptable()` means fish/nu users will get empty substitutions with no error message, which is a silent regression. The fix is a one-line change to `Shell.acceptable()`. - packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts — specifically the `Shell.preferred()` call at line 1817.
